questions.heading: With a Loose M the LP Hires a Sliver of a Contractor
questions.stem: A crew row is written use <= K + M h with M = 2,000 crew-months, and hiring (h = 1) costs a fee of 600. In the LP relaxation, the best plan uses 50 crew-months more than K. What fee does the LP pay for that row?

options.text: 600, since any use over the limit always hires a whole contractor
options.says: In the LP h may be a fraction; it only needs h >= 50 / 2,000.

options.text: 0, since the LP always leaves h at 0 when M is large
options.says: The row needs h >= 50 / 2,000, so h cannot be 0.

options.text: 12, since the LP pays the fee divided by the crew-months over
options.says: The LP pays F / M per crew-month over: 600 / 2,000 times 50.

options.text: 15, since the LP pays the fee times the share 50 / 2,000

questions.heading: A Loose M Weakens the LP Bound; the MILP Optimum Does Not Move
questions.stem: A maximization model has a tight, valid M in each switched row. A colleague replaces every one of them with 1e6, which is also valid. When both versions are solved, what is different?

options.text: The MILP optimum rises, since a larger M allows more plans
options.says: A valid M never changes which plans are allowed, so the best plan is the same.

options.text: The LP bound can only rise, since every allowed plan stays the same
options.says: Right: the LP pays less for breaking each rule, so its bound rises or stays; the plans allowed, and so the MILP optimum, are the same.

options.text: The LP bound falls, since a larger M makes every row harder
options.says: A larger M makes each switched row easier for a fractional switch to satisfy, so the bound cannot fall.

options.text: Nothing at all, since presolve always repairs a loose M
options.says: Presolve repaired the rows on one GridCap run; with presolve off the same loose M took 662 nodes against 32.

questions.heading: A Huge M Lets the Integrality Tolerance Switch a Rule Off
questions.stem: A row reads use <= 20 + M h with M = 5e7. The solver reports OPTIMAL and returns h = 4e-7, which it counts as 0. By how much can use exceed 20 in the returned plan?

options.text: By up to 20, since M times h gives 20 units of room
options.says: Right: 4e-7 times 5e7 is 20, and the row allows it even though h counts as 0.

options.text: By nothing, since OPTIMAL means h is exactly 0
options.says: OPTIMAL holds within tolerances; h = 4e-7 is counted as 0 without being 0.

options.text: By up to 50, since the tolerance times M is the room
options.says: The room comes from the h the solver returned, 4e-7, not from the largest h the tolerance would accept.

options.text: By under 1, since a tolerance never adds a whole unit
options.says: Multiplied by a huge M, a value inside the tolerance gave whole crew-months of room on GridCap.
